officialLinks.label: Grading system, GPA calculation and precision

helpIntro: Georgia Tech uses a 4.0 scale: A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0. Enter credit hours and final grades to estimate your undergraduate institutional GPA.
helpNote: S/U, audit, incomplete, withdrawal, NR/IJ and transfer grades are excluded. Georgia Tech truncates the official GPA after two decimals; this calculator shows three decimals for planning. Repeat Impact is only an estimate for an approved undergraduate grade substitution.
helpExample: A 3-credit A earns 12 quality points and a 4-credit B earns 12. Together, 24 ÷ 7 = 3.428…; Georgia Tech’s official reported GPA is truncated to 3.42.

gradeExplanations.A: A = 4 quality points per credit hour.
gradeExplanations.B: B = 3 quality points per credit hour.
gradeExplanations.C: C = 2 quality points per credit hour.
gradeExplanations.D: D = 1 quality point per credit hour; eligible as an original undergraduate grade-substitution grade when all policy conditions are met.
gradeExplanations.F: F = 0 quality points; attempted credit hours remain in the GPA denominator unless an approved grade substitution removes the original attempt.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete is excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.NR: Not Reported is excluded until a final grade is entered.
gradeExplanations.IJ: Incomplete Judicial is a temporary placeholder and is excluded until a permanent grade is assigned.

specialTypes.name: Georgia Tech course
specialTypes.note: Use final Georgia Tech course grade and credit hours.

specialTypes.name: Transfer or transient credit
specialTypes.note: Accepted non-resident credit can count toward degree/pace, but external grades do not enter the Georgia Tech GPA.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact estimates an approved undergraduate grade substitution only. It does not confirm eligibility, the two-course lifetime limit, misconduct status, deadlines, or whether substitution has been processed. Without approved substitution, enter both attempts as completed courses.
